stem: The Civil Service Commission is made up of a Chairman and two Commissioners, appointed by the President with the consent of the Commission on Appointments. Under Article IX-B, Section 1 of the 1987 Constitution, what is their regular term of office?
hints: There are two things to check: the number of years, and whether the same person can be appointed again.
Article IX-B, Section 1 says the Chairman and the Commissioners are appointed "for a term of ... years without reappointment." Find the number.
The same section gave shorter terms only to the very first members appointed under the 1987 Constitution. Use the regular term, and keep the words that follow it.

solution.methodName: Line up the ages and terms by office

steps.action: Find the rule: the Chairman and the Commissioners are appointed "for a term of seven years without reappointment."
steps.why: "Without reappointment" means a person can serve only one term in the Commission.

steps.action: Set aside the five-year and three-year terms in the same section.
steps.why: Those applied only to "those first appointed": the first Chairman served seven years, one Commissioner five years, and another three years. This way their terms ended in different years.

steps.action: Note the vacancy rule: a person appointed to a vacancy serves "only for the unexpired term of the predecessor."
steps.why: So filling a vacancy does not start a fresh seven-year term.

steps.action: The regular term is seven years, without reappointment.

trapNotes.Six years, without reappointment: Six years is the term of a Senator (Article VI, Section 4) and of the President (Article VII, Section 4). Members of the Civil Service Commission serve seven years.
trapNotes.Seven years, with one reappointment: The number is right, but Section 1 says "without reappointment." A member serves only one term.
trapNotes.Five years, with one reappointment: Five years was only for one of the first Commissioners appointed under the 1987 Constitution, and Section 1 does not allow reappointment.
